idiom_name: declaration-merged Request augmentation (req.user: Principal) plus AsyncLocalStorage for code off the request path
implementation_notes: TypeScript's contribution is making the JavaScript carrier statically typed: declaration merging extends the framework's request type (declare global { namespace Express { interface Request { user?: Principal } } }), so every guard reads a narrowed Principal and the compiler tracks its presence through the handler. The runtime carrier stays JavaScript's - middleware decorates the request, or a NestJS request-scoped provider injects it via the REQUEST token - and code that runs off the request path uses AsyncLocalStorage, whose store is typed as SecurityContext | undefined and must be checked because it does not cross worker_threads or processes. The classic context class is replaced by the typed request property plus the ambient store; keep the property optional and single-sourced, and narrow it in one helper so no guard duplicates the null check.
pitfalls: An optional req.user type-checks even when the authentication middleware is not mounted, so the guard is the enforced boundary - fail closed in one place and reuse it everywhere.
Declaration merging is global: augmenting Express.Request leaks into every file (and can collide with @types/passport), so keep the property optional and define it once in a .d.ts.
AsyncLocalStorage stores are per async resource and do not cross worker_threads or processes: re-bind the context at each boundary instead of assuming it travelled.
